alalal-e89366-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 7: on the diversity and differences of the creeds.

alalal-e89366-d1e113.summary: States the fourth problem: the differences of the creeds.

alalal-e89366-d1e120.summary: Lists seven questions: the origin of the word 'symbolum'; why these two creeds are specially approved; why the Apostles' Creed is called greater though shorter; why it is said twice daily, at Prime and Compline, while the Fathers' Creed is said only on Sundays at Mass after the Gospel; why the one is said silently and the other aloud; why some say the Athanasian Creed weekly at Prime; and whether more creeds and explicit articles can be made if the same cause arises.

alalal-e89366-d1e173.summary: On the name: Cassian says 'symbolum' means collation, the Apostles having gathered into one the faith of the whole catholic law, so that what is spread through all Scripture is collected in perfect brevity, the 'abbreviated word' of Romans 9:28. Contemporary masters derive it from 'syn' and 'bole', sentences of divine truth gathered together.
claims: The creed gathers the sense of all Scripture into a brief summary.

alalal-e89366-d1e230.summary: On approval: Ambrose says the Apostles' Creed is the exemplar of all by its authors' authority; the Nicene matches in figure the number of its Fathers, 318, like Abraham's servants who pursued the enemies and freed Lot, as the Fathers routed the enemies of faith and freed the people captured by heretics. Or because the Nicene contained fewer doubtful points than the Antiochene.

alalal-e89366-d1e272.summary: The Apostles' Creed is called greater because of its authors' authority and because all other creeds interpret it, adding nothing but explaining what was in it.
claims: All later creeds explain the Apostles' Creed without adding to it.

alalal-e89366-d1e288.summary: The greater creed is said twice daily, signifying the two times its remembrance is needed in the Church, at its beginning and at the end against Antichrist, and in a person's life, at receiving the sacraments and at death; and at the first hour of day, to guard the whole day, and the first hour of night at Compline. The Fathers' Creed, an explanation against heresies, is said on Sunday, when people gather and in some lands it is explained in the vernacular; after the Gospel, which confirms it, and before communion, so that unbelievers do not approach the sacrament where faith is at its height, unprovable by reason.

alalal-e89366-d1e359.summary: The Apostles' Creed is said silently because it contains a simple confession that suffices for each person inwardly, and because its authors were in fear behind closed doors; the Fathers' Creed is said aloud because it explains the faith against the clamour of heretics, and was issued when the Church's freedom prevailed.

alalal-e89366-d1e403.summary: The Athanasian Creed chiefly explains, or rather uproots, Arian perfidy and expounds at length all that is in the Nicene, so it is sung at Prime so that the following Mass may be understood from it.

alalal-e89366-d1e422.summary: If necessity pressed, the pope, convening a council of the learned and invoking the Holy Spirit, could explain something implicit in the Apostles' Creed and place it among explicit articles; this would not be inventing a new article but explaining one that always existed, as Anselm says in De processione Spiritus sancti.
claims: The pope with a council can make explicit an article implicit in the Apostles' Creed, without creating a new article.

alalal-e89366.summary: Article 7 treats the differences among the creeds in seven questions. 'Symbolum' means a collation, the Apostles having gathered the sense of all Scripture into a brief word. The Apostles' Creed is the exemplar by its authors' authority, and the Nicene was approved by the figure of its 318 Fathers and its clarity. The Apostles' Creed is greater because all other creeds only explain it. Albert explains their liturgical use: the Apostles' Creed is said silently twice daily, at Prime and Compline, as a simple personal confession first made in fear; the Nicene is said aloud on Sundays after the Gospel and before communion, as the Church's public explanation against heresy; the Athanasian is said at Prime as an exposition against Arianism. In necessity the pope with a council could make explicit what is implicit in the Apostles' Creed, which would explain an old article rather than create a new one.
claims: The Apostles' Creed is the exemplar of all creeds, which only explain it.
The creeds' liturgical uses reflect their character as simple confession or public refutation of heresy.
The pope with a council can make explicit an article implicit in the Apostles' Creed, without creating a new article.
